# `MountUpdate`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Mount-controller firmware write worker state.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER (observation only; receiving the event changes nothing) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, StartWritemountBoot @0x11ac70, LoadHotSetting start-up trigger @0x11b5c0-0x11b840, MainArgHandle trigger @0x11b10c, WriteMountBootFunc @0x136ab0, function-name initializer @0x9d360, SendFuncEvent @0x6e4e20 (64-bit build); 32-bit start path equivalent; no wire observation |

F family with no task-specific members (the detail has no formatter, so no percent, file name or numeric progress is proved). Sent by the mount-boot write worker once it starts successfully, following its lifecycle; no periodic progress timer is established. The F serializer supports idle, working, complete, fail and cancel; that is not a guarantee that every state, or a successful flash, is reached on every model. The worker has no model check. It starts at imager start-up when the device has the flashing tool installed, no done-marker exists for this boot, and the persisted write_mountboot flag is set; it can also start from a start-up command-line option. READ. It puts the mount controller into boot mode and flashes it over a fixed serial port, retrying; on a verified write it clears the flag and writes the marker, so it runs at most once per flag setting. READ. A client cannot start it through the control API. Which models ship the tool and set the flag is a firmware-packaging matter and unresolved. Broadcast on TCP 4700 to every retained socket. No wire observation exists and no APK consumer is established.

Side effects: None for the receiver. The worker it reports writes mount-controller firmware.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"MountUpdate"`. [READ] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string with nine fractional digits from a monotonic clock; not a calendar time. [READ] |
| `state` | string | yes | - | F state table: idle 0, working 1, complete 2, fail 3, cancel 4; an unknown internal code falls back to idle. A formatter's supported state is not a promise that every run visits it. One of: `idle`, `working`, `complete`, `fail`, `cancel`. [READ] |
| `stage` | string | if a non-empty stage string is held | - | Only when a non-empty stage string is held. [READ] |
| `lapse_ms` | integer | if state is working, or the timer was started (terminal states) | - | Elapsed milliseconds, independent of Timestamp. Working (or started with no end) uses current monotonic minus start; other terminal states use end minus start. [READ] |
| `route` | array<string> | no | - | Ordered function-tree ancestry when included; a missing route is a legitimate branch. Not an address. [READ] |
| `error` | string | if state is fail | - | Message for code; written for state fail even when the stored code is zero. Lookup failure gives 'fail to operate'. Cancel omits it. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | if state is fail | - | Written for state fail, including a stored zero. Cancel omits it. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, working - Write in progress (READ shape; values invented, not captured):

```json
{"Event":"MountUpdate","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"working","lapse_ms":8000}
```

Event, fail - Write failed (READ shape; values invented):

```json
{"Event":"MountUpdate","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"fail","lapse_ms":9000,"error":"fail to operate","code":0}
```
